sentences.text:
THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR FINAL HEARING,
THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:

JUDGMENT Heard Sri Shiva Kumar P., learned counsel for the appellant as well as Sri B.C.Shivanne Gowda,
learned counsel, who is representing Sri B.Pradeep, learned counsel for respondent No.2.
2.
Though Sri Sheshadri S., learned counsel, is on record representing respondent No.1, learned counsel failed to make his submission.

Aggrieved by the sum that was awarded as compensation in favour of the appellant, through orders in M.V.C. No.149/2014, dated 28.04.2015 by the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Hiriyur,
the present appeal is preferred by the claimant.
4. Seeking for enhancement of compensation, learned counsel for appellant made his submission regarding two aspects.
Firstly, that no amount is awarded towards loss of amenities in life.

Secondly,
that the Tribunal failed to award any compensation towards loss of income, during laid up period.
5. Learned counsel appearing for respondent No.2 on the on the other hand, states that the amount awarded as compensation is just and reasonable.
6. Subjecting the evidence of PWs-1 and PW-2, Ex. P-3, P-6 to P-399 to scrutiny, the Tribunal awarded a sum of Rs.20,78,840/- as compensation.

However, a perusal of the impugned order goes to show that no amount is NC: 2023:KHC:45641 awarded under the heads 'loss of amenities in life'
and 'loss of income during laid up period'.
7.
As per the contents of Ex.P-3 wound certificate, the appellant sustained two grievance injuries apart from one simple injury.
The evidence of PW-2, in this regard is that he is a consultant Surgeon at Aditya Orthopedic and Trauma Center, Tumkur.

entities.text: Aditya Orthopedic and Trauma Center, Tumkur
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The appellant was admitted at their Hospital on 13.10.2013.

He was found with comminuted fracture of both bones of right forearm, fracture of Sri. L. Gopalakrishna vs S. Mallikarjuna on 13 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/107246853/

sentences.text: distal femur right and head injury.

He stated that on 01.11.2013, there was external fixators removal on 16.11.2013 ORIF with locking plate for Femur (R) and on 25.11.2013, Girdle Stone Orthoplasty (R) hip and square Nail Removal for Ulna was done.

entities.text: Girdle Stone Orthoplasty (R) hip and square Nail Removal for Ulna
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: He was discharged on 18.12.2013.
However, he was again admitted on 10.01.2014 and discharged on 18.01.2014, admitted on 06.02.2014 and discharged on 21.02.2014 and admitted on 14.03.2014 and discharged on 22.03.2014.

Having considered the gravity of injuries sustained and taking into consideration, the aspect of disability as observed by the Tribunal in the impugned order itself, the Tribunal ought to have awarded certain amount towards loss of amenities in life.
Also having considered nature of injuries sustained, the Court is of the view, that the appellant might not have attended his normal duties for a period of six months.
The Tribunal has taken the income of the appellant as Rs.9,000/- per month.

Thus, the loss of income for a period of six months comes to Rs.54,000/- (Rs.9,000/- x 6).
9.
Also having regard to the nature of injuries sustained reasonable figure that can be awarded towards loss of amenities in life is Rs.25,000/-.
Thus the compensation granted can be enhanced by Rs.79,000/- (25,000+54,000).
Thus, the appeal is allowed in part.
The compensation that is awarded by the Tribunal through the impugned order is enhanced by Rs.79,000/-.
The enhanced amount shall carry interest at the rate as awarded by the Tribunal.
